svg.title: Wave-depth distribution — deep cascades are real for the points-maximizer and nearly absent from survival play
svg.desc: Wave-depth distribution — deep cascades are real for the points-maximizer and nearly absent from survival play. finding-06 section 4 wave-depth table, copied verbatim; share of all waves at each depth per policy. Cohorts: fair D4 (this run), rh-clears H9 and rh-points H9 are 8-game cohorts on the eight master tapes (400-move cap); rh-clears cap-1000 is 6 games on six fresh futures at a 1,000-move cap; the H9 exact optimum column is the 2,249 waves of the 128 suite-h9-v1 optimal lines, a window sample rather than whole games. Waves observed per policy: 1,374 / 5,018 / 9,501 / 2,179 / 2,249 (carried per point). CAVEAT on the bands: 'depth >=15' is a subset of 'depth >=11', not a partition — both rows are charted exactly as recorded. The rh-points tail (21.53% at depth >=11, 7.76% at >=15, deepest 22) is the chain-construction regime that earns 1.75x the points per move and still loses on the mean (1,123,130 vs 1,544,461) because it cuts lifetime by 58%; the survival policies' profiles are near-identical (0.22-0.72% past depth 10). finding-01's independent base-engine measurement (44.0% at depth 1, deepest-ever 11 over 8,444 waves in 64 fair-D4 games) is a different cohort and engine — noted here, not charted. The eight-tape cohort is now known to favour long games (finding-12); this is a descriptive share table, not a lifetime figure. Evidence tier: development/pilot. Sources: docs/exploratory/finding-06-flow-ceiling.md.
